chapter_plans.title: The Offer She Can't Refuse
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane is appointed Lead Forensic Authority for the Meridian Spine and meets Stellan Marsh, Nadia Okafor, and Petra Lund, spotting a tool-mark anomaly in the load coupons that matches a Kessler-era override.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Iris Kane arrives at the National Integrity Directorate headquarters. Stellan Marsh officially welcomes her as Lead Forensic Authority for the Meridian Spine, framing it as the reform's cornerstone. Her designated investigative partner, Nadia Okafor, immediately begins steering her focus toward institutional structure. During a tour of the Spine's fabrication facility, Iris meets Petra Lund, the lead certifier. Lund is nervous, her explanations careful. Iris examines the load coupons and discovers a tool-mark pattern identical to the Kessler override—a physical anomaly she cannot explain away. She hides the observation, guarding it alongside the unresolved redacted page from Book 1.
must_happen: Iris Kane accepts the role of Lead Forensic Authority for the Meridian Spine from Stellan Marsh.
Nadia Okafor is introduced as Iris's partner and subtly directs her attention toward Gerald Halveston's fund.
During a fabrication facility tour, Iris spots a tool-mark in the certified load coupons that matches the Kessler override method (C010 planted).
must_not: Must not reveal that the National Integrity Directorate is a capture instrument.
Must not name Stellan Marsh as the architect of any broader fraud.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "Iris Kane, I need you to certify the spine so clean it squeaks." — Stellan Marsh slides the contract across his glass desk, smiling as if he's doing her a favor.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Iris stares at the load coupon in her private office, the tool-mark matching a Kessler-class override. She holds a single note from her Book 1 files: *Find the other names.*
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The tool-mark on the coupon has a microscopic wave pattern in the shear line — not a standard machining defect, but one created by an override jig that shouldn't exist outside the Kessler scrap pile.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: The weight of the new position pushes against the fracture of the unresolved page. She feels trusted — and guilty for not trusting the institution giving her the trust.

chapter_plans.title: The Revolving Door
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane finds a timestamp discrepancy in the Spine's records, receives suspicious explanations from Petra Lund, and uncovers a missing serial number on the tooling rig.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: During her first official week, Iris delves into the Meridian Spine certification files. She finds a critical discrepancy: a load test was certified before the pre-certification checks were recorded (C001). Petra Lund visits, offering an explanation that feels rehearsed and evasive. Lund mentions receiving specific tooling from an unnamed higher source. Nadia Okafor pressures Iris to meet Gerald Halveston, framing the meeting as essential for political capital. A journalist calls Iris's office, asking directly about the 'unredacted co-owners' of the Kessler fast-track, reopening her old wound. Iris investigates the tooling serial number and discovers it does not exist in the manufacturer's database (C002).
must_happen: Iris identifies a conflict in the Meridian Spine's approval timestamps, suggesting a backdated certification (C001 planted).
Petra Lund's evasive behavior deepens Iris's suspicion of her role.
Iris discovers the serial number for the load test rig's tooling is not registered with the manufacturer (C002 planted).
must_not: Must not confirm the Directorate is a wider capture instrument.
Must not reveal Nadia Okafor's deliberate steering of the investigation.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "The first material I ever certified is still standing," Petra Lund says, knocking her knuckles against the spine section in the showroom. "That means something where I come from."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: The journalist's question loops in Iris's head. *Unresolved co-owners.* She opens the redacted page file from Book 1 again. Renn's trial testimony. 'I was paid by a company. A developer. Ask the developers.'
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The missing serial number feels deliberately erased — not faded or misprinted, but removed from the manufacturer's database with surgical precision.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Iris battles the isolation of her suspicions. Being surrounded by new colleagues in a job that feels like a reward only sharpens her distrust.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Deepen the investigation setup. Plant clues C001 and C002. Build distrust in Lund and Nadia's agendas. No romance subplot. Target length: 1600-1900 words.

chapter_plans.title: The Financier's Compass
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane and Nadia Okafor meet Gerald Halveston, who presents himself as a reform ally, but Iris discovers a shell company—Veridian Trust—linking the Spine's financing to the Kessler era.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Nadia and Iris visit the Halveston Foundation headquarters. Halveston is polished and positions himself as a transparent force for good. He reveals he vetted Iris personally, unsettling her. Iris notices Halveston is deeply invested in the Spine's narrative but avoids technical details. During the meeting, the contract structure surfaces: a shell company called Veridian Trust provides the real financing, with no public reporting requirements. Nadia frames Halveston as the primary political target. Iris leaves the meeting suspecting she is being directed toward a false wall. Later, she searches for Veridian Trust and finds its registration predates the Kessler collapse, sharing an address with Renn's old backers.
must_happen: Iris and Nadia meet Gerald Halveston at the Halveston Foundation.
Halveston implies he vetted Iris personally, revealing how closely she is being managed.
Iris discovers the Veridian Trust shell company structure behind the Meridian Spine financing.
must_not: Must not reveal Halveston's exact coordinating role (only implied false wall).
Must not connect the dots to Marsh as the architect.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "My grandfather built bridges you can still walk across," Halveston says, shaking Iris's hand. "I build the bridges that keep those bridges standing. Software of accountability."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Iris searches for the Veridian Trust's registration number. It was registered six months before the Kessler collapse. The co-owners of Renn's old company and the founders of this trust share a legal address.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The Veridian Trust letterhead has the same corporate logo kerning as the redacted bottom of the Kessler page — same typehouse, same who-are-you-hiding.

chapter_plans.title: The Executor's Purchase
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane confronts Petra Lund with the tool-mark match, and traces the supplier behind Lund's override jig to a Veridian Trust subsidiary.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Iris Kane invites Petra Lund to her office and presents the micrograph evidence. Lund initially denies, but breaks when Iris shows the serial number gap. Lund admits she used the override jig but claims she was following instructions from the certification committee and did not know the tooling was fraudulent. She provides the supplier name, Aegis Fabrication. Iris investigates the Aegis purchase order and finds it was pushed through an informal vendor list. She uses the missing serial number (C002 payoff) to trace the tooling to Aegis. A new email (C003) from an internal whistleblower shows that Aegis was acquired by Veridian Trust after the Spine contract was awarded. This minor reveal (MR001) solidifies a link between Lund's fraud and the shell company financing the Spine.
must_happen: Iris Kane confronts Petra Lund and forces her to admit the override method and name the tooling supplier Aegis Fabrication.
Iris Kane verifies that the serial number missing from the manufacturer's database (C002) corresponds to the Aegis jig.
Iris Kane receives an internal email showing Aegis was acquired by Veridian Trust after the Meridian Spine contract (C003 payoff, MR001).
must_not: Must not state that Stellan Marsh architected the National Integrity Directorate as a capture instrument.
Must not have Iris fully trust Nadia Okafor or believe she is not steering the investigation.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "The fracture on the Spine coupon matches the Kessler override at every point," Iris Kane says, placing the micrograph on Petra Lund's desk. "I need to know who gave you the jig."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: As Iris returns to her office after the confrontation, she finds a typed note under the door: 'You're looking at the wrong supplier. Veridian Trust acquired Aegis after the fact. The real tooling vendor is still inside the Directorate. — A friend.'
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The Aegis Fabrication purchase order is printed on paper with a watermark of a Latin phrase Iris recognizes from the Kessler files, hinting at a shared legal counsel.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: The satisfaction of cracking Lund is undercut by the realization that Iris is still a step behind — someone else is guiding the investigation even when she exposes the executor.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Advance the evidence chain from Lund to Veridian Trust. Pay off clues C002 and C003, minor reveal MR001. Keep focus on physical evidence, no romance. Target length: 1600-1900 words.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Iris has a new lead: the insider note points to a vendor inside the Directorate, not Aegis. She will investigate who inside the Directorate certified Aegis.

chapter_plans.title: The Inside Vendor
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane investigates the Directorate employee who approved Aegis Fabrication, but finds her path blocked by Nadia Okafor and a missing evidence file.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Iris Kane begins tracing the procurement trail. She identifies the Directorate employee who personally approved Aegis Fabrication as a qualified vendor: Alan Torvik, a procurement officer in the major projects division. She arranges a meeting with him, but he is suddenly on leave. When she pushes, she is told by his assistant that his files have been moved to legal. She suspects the evidence is being hidden. Nadia Okafor confronts her, directly warning her not to involve Directorate personnel in an investigation meant for external actors. Iris is now sure that Nadia is protecting someone inside. She also receives a call from the Directorate legal department informing her that her investigation scope is limited to the Spine certification, and further personnel inquiries require Stellan Marsh's approval. Frustrated, Iris visits the records room and finds that her original micrograph of the coupon has been removed from the evidence locker.
must_happen: Iris Kane identifies procurement officer Alan Torvik as the approver of Aegis Fabrication and attempts to interview him.
Nadia Okafor warns Iris to focus on external actors, confirming she is being steered away from internal figures.
Iris Kane discovers her micrograph evidence has been tampered with or removed from the locker.
must_not: Must not reveal Stellan Marsh's role as architect of any broader fraud.
Must not have Iris draw a direct line from internal obstruction to Stellan Marsh personally.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "You need to stop digging into our own procurement," Nadia Okafor says, her voice low. "The Directorate is the institution that needs to survive, not your private investigation."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Iris storms to the evidence locker. The slide tray is empty. Her micrograph, her only physical proof of the tool-mark match, is gone. She stands in the stark light, knowing that someone inside the Directorate has taken it.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The empty slide tray is dusted with a fine white powder — fingerprint powder — indicating a deliberate removal by someone who knew exactly what they were taking.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: The isolation closes in. Iris has been trusted, celebrated, and now contains a trap: the cell is her office, the guards are her allies.

chapter_plans.title: The Source in Ironwood
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane visits Aldous Renn in prison, receives a cryptic warning about the procurement system itself, and is summoned to Stellan Marsh's office — ending Act 1.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Without the micrograph, Iris Kane re-documents her analysis from memory and sketches the tool-mark pattern. She decides to reach out to the one person who might know how the override method survived: Aldous Renn. In prison, Renn is cool and observant. He asks why she is still chasing the method when she should be chasing the system that allowed it. He hints that the people who funded him are now inside the Directorate, and that the certification rules were rewritten after Kessler to accommodate the pattern. He warns her that exposing them will cost her everything, but she presses. Renn gives her a name: the law firm that drafted the Veridian Trust charter — same firm that represented his shell companies. Iris leaves unsettled. On her way out of the prison parking lot, she gets a call from the Directorate's central office: Stellan Marsh requests a meeting with her first thing in the morning.
must_happen: Iris Kane visits Aldous Renn in prison and extracts a lead: the law firm behind Veridian Trust also worked for Renn's companies.
Stellan Marsh's office officially summons Iris for a private meeting the next day.
Iris Kane realizes that her evidence chain, though damaged, now connects Lund to the same legal origins as Renn's network.
must_not: Must not state that Stellan Marsh architected the National Integrity Directorate as a capture instrument.
Must not have Renn explicitly name Marsh or Halveston as the active architects.
